# f5xc_service_policy_rule (Resource)

service policy rule object A service_policy_rule object consists of an unordered list of predicates and an action. The predicates are evaluated against a set of input fields that are extracted from or derived from an L7 request API. A request API is considered to match a rule if all predicates in the rule evaluate to true for that request. Any predicates that are not specified in a rule are implicitly considered to be true. If a request API matches a rule, the action specified for the rule is enforced for that request. A service_policy_rule can be part of exactly one service_policy and must belong to the same namespace as the service policy.

To get more information about f5xc_service_policy_rule, refer:

- [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.f5.com/docs-v2/api/service-policy-rule)

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--tls_fingerprint_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tls_fingerprint_choice`

Optional:

- `ja4_tls_fingerprint` (Attributes) ja4 tls fingerprint An extended version of JA3 that includes additional fields for more comprehensive fingerprinting of SSL/TLS clients and potentially has a different structure and length. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tls_fingerprint_choice--ja4_tls_fingerprint))
- `tls_fingerprint_matcher` (Attributes) TLS JA3 fingerprint matcher A method for uniquely identifying SSL/TLS clients by creating a 32-character MD5 hash based on the parameters of the Client Hello packet during the handshake. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tls_fingerprint_choice--tls_fingerprint_matcher))

<a id="nestedatt--tls_fingerprint_choice--ja4_tls_fingerprint"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tls_fingerprint_choice.ja4_tls_fingerprint`

Optional:

- `exact_values` (List of String) exact values A list of exact JA4 TLS fingerprint to match the input JA4 TLS fingerprint against


<a id="nestedatt--tls_fingerprint_choice--tls_fingerprint_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tls_fingerprint_choice.tls_fingerprint_matcher`

Optional:

- `classes` (List of String) classes A list of known classes of TLS fingerprints to match the input TLS JA3 fingerprint against.<br>**Valid Options:** `['ADWARE', 'ADWIND', 'ANY_MALICIOUS_FINGERPRINT', 'DRIDEX', 'GOOTKIT', 'GOZI', 'JBIFROST', 'QUAKBOT', 'RANSOMWARE', 'TOFSEE', 'TORRENTLOCKER', 'TRICKBOT', 'TROLDESH']` (Multiple selection allowed)<br>**Default:** `TLS_FINGERPRINT_NONE`
- `exact_values` (List of String) exact values A list of exact TLS JA3 fingerprints to match the input TLS JA3 fingerprint against.
- `excluded_values` (List of String) excluded values A list of TLS JA3 fingerprints to be excluded when matching the input TLS JA3 fingerprint. This can be used to skip known false positives when using one or more known TLS fingerprint classes in the enclosing matcher.
## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an `import` block to import this resource by ID.

> **Note:** Replace placeholder values (for example, `<namespace>`, `<name>`) with actual values.

### Command-Line Import

Use the following `command` to import this resource from the command line:

```shell
terraform import f5xc_service_policy_rule.example <namespace>/<name>
```

### HCL Import Block

Use the following `hcl` block to import this resource during `plan` or `apply`:

```hcl
import {
	id = "<namespace>/<name>"
	to = "f5xc_service_policy_rule.example"
}
```
